source.title: ReSAE: Residualized Sparse Autoencoders for Multi-Layer Transformer Interventions
source.authors: Prathyush Poduval; Calvin Yeung; Neel Desai; Mohsen Imani

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies affine predictability between different transformer layers and the effects of replacing activations with SAE reconstructions. It does not measure the SAE reconstruction error's linear predictability from its own input, per-token error scaling or overlap across SAE sizes, or the other specified dark-matter properties.
record.gate_note: The paper reports affine cross-layer regression results, but these concern prediction of a later layer's activation from an earlier layer, not SAE reconstruction error. Its SAE-replacement cross-entropy comparisons are recorded as related findings, but there is no same-size random-error comparison or test of retaining the error term. Other reported metrics are not measurements of the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper introduces ReSAEs, which train SAEs on affine cross-layer residuals, and compares them with raw SAEs on EV, decoder redundancy, multi-layer CE replacement, probing, TPP and SCR. It never measures the SAE error vector's linear predictability from its own input. It has no error-norm scaling across dictionary sizes (N is fixed at 65,536), no same-norm random-error baseline, and no test of keeping the error term in circuits or steering. It also does not decompose dark matter. It does not cite or discuss the dark-matter paper. 'discusses' is the nearest available relation; in substance the study neither tests nor uses the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that affine residualization reduces decoder redundancy and improves multi-layer CE recovery, sparse probing and TPP. The gains are not universal: SCR favours raw SAEs on Pythia, and low-k online replacement favours raw SAEs.
record.recipe_differences: This is not a reproduction of the dark-matter measurements. It trains BatchTopK SAEs on affine residuals between selected layers and evaluates multi-layer replacement, feature readout, and ablations.
record.method_sensitivity: For the reported reconstruction interventions, results vary with sparsity, replacement mode, and (for Gemma) layer spacing. Pythia online replacement favors raw SAEs at very low sparsity but ReSAEs at k = 160 and 320; Gemma ReSAEs perform better across the tested gaps.

fits_no_version.finding: ReSAEs have lower original-space EV than raw SAEs (0.780–0.864 vs 0.823–0.902) but recover more CE under multi-layer replacement. Examples: Pythia teacher-forced CE 2.398 at k=320 versus a clean CE of 2.260; Gemma sequential-online ΔCE 0.743–1.093 vs 1.591–2.371. Raw SAEs do better online at low k on Pythia.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training SAEs on affine cross-layer residuals improves CE recovery under multi-layer replacement relative to raw SAEs, despite lower explained variance, given sufficient sparsity budget.

record.problems: The study covers two model families and a limited set of layer configurations. It reports no uncertainty estimates for these comparisons and includes no same-size random-error baseline, so its cross-entropy results do not directly test the specified pathological-error comparison.
record.rows_left_out: Other reported results, including affine cross-layer regression, explained variance, decoder similarity, overinteraction, sparse probing, targeted perturbation, and spurious-correlation removal, were left out because they do not measure a claim version's specified SAE-error property. Per-gap Gemma cross-entropy values are figure-only and retained as separate rows; exact values are not stated in the text.

untested.parts: Share of SAE error linearly predictable from the same-layer input activation. The affine regression R² in Fig. 1 predicts a later layer's activation from an earlier layer, not SAE error.
Per-token error-norm prediction across SAE sizes, overlap of failure contexts, and persistence of error with scale. Dictionary size is fixed.
SAE-reconstruction CE harm compared with random errors of the same norm.
Splitting error into linear and nonlinear parts, and whether each resists further dictionary learning.
Behaviour lost by SAE-feature circuits or steering unless the error term is kept.
Whether dark matter shrinks with better architectures or training. ReSAE versus raw SAE compares CE and EV, not the size or structure of the error components.

record.verdict_notes: The rows are correctly linked to no version. The study does not cite arXiv:2410.14670. Its 'linearly predictable' structure is cross-layer activation structure, not the SAE error's predictability from its own input. It should not be read as bearing on V1 or V4.

versions.untested_parts: Whether SAE error vectors are linearly predictable from their own input activations, and what share of error this explains.
Per-token error-norm predictability across SAE sizes, whether larger SAEs fail on the same contexts, and whether error persists with scale.
Whether SAE reconstruction replacement harms loss more than random errors of the same size.
Whether the linear error component corresponds to unlearned features and the nonlinear component resists further dictionary learning.
Whether analyses based on SAE features lose behavior unless the error term is retained.
Whether dark matter is mainly an SAE-training artifact or shrinks with better architectures or end-to-end training.
